answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce-token deposit before placing jobs or claiming rewards, then slash deposits when audits prove fraud. A sybil attacker must spread capital across many identities and risks losing each stake, making fake accounts costly rather than free. The ocean of possible identities is constrained by funds; a river of accounts cannot multiply influence without more capital, and the zenith of the attack is bounded by the attacker’s budget.
